title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 758 of the 'suite' of La Longue Marche, §4: 'approximation de Lie de (Π_0, 𝔊_0, M)', meaning a Lie or algebraic-group approximation induced by an approximation of 𝔊_0.

The setting:
- 𝔊_0 is a discrete LT-group. It carries an 'LT-structure', a family of homomorphisms K_i : T_0 → 𝔊_0 (i ∈ I) defined up to conjugacy. Here T_0 ≅ ℤ and the images are the 'lacets', i.e. inertia or Dehn-twist type subgroups.
- Π_0 is a normal L-subgroup. The model case is a mapping class or braid group (Teichmüller modular group) containing a surface fundamental group.
- Marginal hypothesis: the multiplier character 𝔊_0 → ℤ* = {±1}, given by the action on the L-group Π_0, is trivial. This is the discrete analogue of the cyclotomic character, so it amounts to an orientation-preserving hypothesis.

The data assumed:
- An affine group scheme 𝔊_ℚ over ℚ.
- A homomorphism φ : 𝔊_0 → 𝔊(ℚ) (65) such that every composite T_0 → 𝔊_0 → 𝔊(ℚ) is quasi-unipotent. This is the analogue of the monodromy theorem: Dehn twists go to quasi-unipotent elements.
- 𝔊_ℚ is generated by the ℚ-points coming from 𝔊_0, i.e. φ has Zariski-dense image.

The construction:
- 𝔊_ℚ is then regarded as an 'algebraic LT-group'. It is equipped with φ and with outer homomorphisms K̲_i : T̲_0,ℚ → 𝔊_ℚ (67). These extend the K_i through the algebraic hull of T_0 (for unipotent images, the Malcev completion 𝔾_a), with the compatibility square (68) on the next page.
- On the next page he defines the group scheme M^φ_ℚ of pairs (u, μ). Here u is an automorphism of 𝔊_ℚ and μ ∈ 𝔾_m. For each i the condition is u(K̲_i(λ)) = int(f_i)^{-1}(μλ), with f_i a local section of Π̲_ℚ (the Zariski closure of φ(Π_0)).
- So u sends each loop subgroup to a Π-conjugate of its 'μ-th power'. This is exactly the defining condition of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (inertia preserved up to conjugacy, with the cyclotomic twist), transposed to the algebraic/Lie setting over ℚ with 𝔾_m in place of ℤ̂*.
- Inner automorphisms from 𝔊_ℚ lie in the kernel of the character. Hence there is a quotient Γ^φ_ℚ = M^φ_ℚ / Im 𝔊_ℚ with a character χ_Γ to 𝔾_m (70). This is a ℚ-algebraic 'GT-type' group attached to any Zariski-dense quasi-unipotent representation of the Teichmüller-type group.
- The page breaks off where it begins to apply this to a 'système de Teichmüller', presumably to get a tower of such groups and a map from Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) or ĜT.

Purpose: to linearise the anabelian/GT problem. The profinite Teichmüller tower and its automorphism group (the analogue of ĜT) is replaced by algebraic group approximations, such as Malcev or relative completions, where Lie-algebra methods apply.
errors: Gap: quasi-unipotent (not unipotent) images of T_0 ≅ ℤ do not extend to a homomorphism from the Malcev completion 𝔾_a. T̲_0,ℚ must be understood as an algebraic hull of the form (finite cyclic) × 𝔾_a, or one must pass to a finite-index subgroup. The page does not specify which.
M^φ_ℚ as described ('inf/dim', automorphisms of a possibly non-finite-type group scheme) is in general only a pro-algebraic or ind-object. Representability is not addressed.
Minor: the condition uses 'μλ' additively, which makes sense only on the unipotent part of T̲_0,ℚ.

ideas.what: Approximating a discrete Teichmüller-type group by a Zariski-dense representation into a ℚ-algebraic group in which loops/Dehn twists become quasi-unipotent, then treating the image as an algebraic LT-group.
ideas.modern_name: Relative (Malcev) completion / weighted completion of mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (suggestion), R. Hain (relative completion, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme in this form; the earlier parts of La Longue Marche (1981) discuss profinite and Malcev aspects, but this 'suite' is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Group scheme over ℚ of automorphisms of the algebraic approximation preserving each loop subgroup up to Π-conjugacy and a common scalar twist μ ∈ 𝔾_m, modulo inner automorphisms, with a character to 𝔾_m.
ideas.modern_name: Pro-unipotent / ℚ-algebraic Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (GT(ℚ), GRT-type) for relative completions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for the unipotent GT over ℚ; Deligne (1989) for motivic unipotent π_1; Hain–Matsumoto for relative versions

ideas.what: Hypothesis that the multiplier (orientation) character to {±1} is trivial, as the discrete analogue of the cyclotomic character.
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche discussions of multipliers

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in generality, a ℚ-algebraic GT-type group Γ^φ_ℚ → 𝔾_m attached to any Zariski-dense representation of a Teichmüller-type group with quasi-unipotent Dehn twists, not just the unipotent completion. The thread is to compare such groups across a Teichmüller system. This anticipates Hain–Matsumoto's relative/weighted completions and the Galois/GT actions on them, but phrased as a GT-type automorphism group defined purely by loop data.
missed.quote: approximation de Lie de (Π_0, 𝔊_0, M) (induite par une approximation de 𝔊_0) ... soit quasi-unipotent ... 𝔊_ℚ soit engendré par l'ens des pts ℚ-rationnels
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: GT-type groups for relative completions of mapping class groups (e.g. relative to Sp_2g) are studied mainly through Galois or motivic images (Hain, Matsumoto, Brown). A combinatorially defined 'relative GT' via loop-preservation, as here, is less systematically developed and could give an upper bound for those images.

missed.claim: The page links the anabelian profinite GT programme with algebraic-group/Lie approximations (Malcev, relative completion), years before Deligne (1989) and Drinfeld (1990) made the unipotent ℚ-version standard.
missed.quote: On considère 𝔊_ℚ comme muni de l'homomorphisme (65) et de la famille des homomorphismes extérieurs (67)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: Grothendieck had the algebraic-group version of GT in view in the early 1980s.

deep.surprise_reason: An explicit, general definition of a ℚ-algebraic GT-type group attached to a Zariski-dense quasi-unipotent representation (relative-completion style) is a notable unpublished anticipation of Drinfeld's GT(ℚ) and Hain's relative completions. The page is only a setup, though, and the ideas were later developed independently.
transcription_corrections: Header: '758' is the page number of the series; the title reads 'approximation de Lie de (Π_0, 𝔊_0, M)', with 'hom' struck out and 'de (Π_0, 𝔊_0, M)' added above.
The second displayed homomorphism is labelled (66), not (65): '(66) K_i : T_0 → 𝔊_0'.

Marginal note (written diagonally in the left margin): 'On suppose que l'hom 𝔊_0 → ℤ* = {±1} défini par l'action de 𝔊_0 sur le L-groupe Π_0 (i.e. multiplicateurs) soit trivial...' — the transcription's rendering is essentially correct.
'Supposons donné [un] schéma en groupes 𝔊_ℚ sur ℚ' — the article 'un' is lost at the line break.
